name: Nitrofurantoin
route_note: Oral capsules (macrocrystals or modified-release) or suspension, taken with food.
targets: Bacterial nitroreductases (nfsA, nfsB) generating reactive intermediates that damage ribosomes, DNA and metabolic enzymes

discovery.note: One of several antibacterial nitrofurans developed in the 1940s–50s.

tagline: Urine-concentrated nitrofuran, a first-line treatment for cystitis
summary: Nitrofurantoin is a synthetic nitrofuran used since 1953 to treat and prevent uncomplicated lower urinary tract infections. It reaches therapeutic concentrations only in urine, so it is unsuitable for pyelonephritis or systemic infections, and resistance has remained low despite decades of use.
mechanism: Nitrofurantoin is a prodrug reduced by bacterial flavoprotein nitroreductases (NfsA and NfsB in E. coli) to highly reactive electrophilic intermediates. These attack ribosomal proteins, DNA, and enzymes of the citric acid cycle and cell-wall synthesis, so many targets are hit at once.

This multi-target action is thought to explain the low rate of acquired resistance, which usually requires stepwise loss of both nitroreductases. Rapid renal excretion produces high urinary but negligible plasma concentrations.
uses: Prophylaxis of recurrent urinary tract infections
Lower urinary tract infections in pregnancy (avoided near term)

history.title: Nitrofurans
history.detail: Antibacterial activity of nitrofuran compounds is reported by Dodd and Stillman.

history.title: Introduction
history.detail: Nitrofurantoin is introduced in the US as Furadantin.

history.title: Modified-release
history.detail: Macrobid twice-daily capsules are approved in the US.

history.title: IDSA guideline
history.detail: IDSA/ESCMID guidelines name nitrofurantoin a first-line agent for acute uncomplicated cystitis.

history.title: Beers criteria revised
history.detail: The American Geriatrics Society relaxes its renal cut-off, advising avoidance mainly when creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min.

history.title: NICE guidance
history.detail: NICE guideline NG109 recommends nitrofurantoin first-line for lower UTI when kidney function allows.

pk.bioavailability: about 40–90% depending on formulation; increased by food

serious: Chronic pulmonary fibrosis with long-term use
Haemolytic anaemia in G6PD deficiency and in neonates

facts: Nitrofurantoin efficacy depends on adequate kidney function to concentrate the drug in urine.
